title: Two independent, un-synchronized migration-tracking tables for tenant schemas cause spurious "already exists" DDL failures on fresh test DBs
summary: Discovered while verifying the ISS-0090 (GitHub #339) fix against a live integration test run. tests/integration/helpers.zig's own runMigrationsForSchema() maintains a legacy, schema-local schema_migrations table (physically inside each tenant schema, e.g. tenant_default.schema_migrations) that is completely independent from the canonical public.schema_migrations(schema_name, version) table that src/db/migrations.zig::Migrations.runForSchema() uses -- the tracker ISS-504 (GitHub #204, closed just before this issue was filed) explicitly decided should be the single source of truth (see src/design/iss504_migration_tracking.md, 'Decision: Do NOT create a separate per-tenant schema_migrations table'). Because both trackers apply the same migrations/*.sql files to the same tenant_default schema but consult different bookkeeping, migration 047_repository_form_schemas.sql (creates form_schema_registry with CONSTRAINT uq_form_schema_field UNIQUE) is recorded as applied in the harness's local tenant_default.schema_migrations table but has no corresponding row in public.schema_migrations WHERE schema_name='tenant_default' (verified: only 46 of ~94 migrations recorded there vs. all ~94 in the harness's local copy). A later migration (072_tnt01_rename_legacy_tables.sql) idempotently renames form_schema_registry to repository_form_schemas but leaves the uq_form_schema_field constraint/index name attached (Postgres does not rename constraints on ALTER TABLE RENAME). Any test file whose makePool() calls the real Migrations.runForSchema() directly (bypassing TestHarness -- e.g. tests/integration/iss102_claim_test.zig:93-115) sees migration 047 as NOT applied per its own tracker and re-attempts CREATE TABLE form_schema_registry ... CONSTRAINT uq_form_schema_field UNIQUE, which fails because that index name already exists (attached to the renamed table). Reproduces deterministically on a single-threaded, single-process, byte-fresh db_test container/volume -- it is NOT a concurrency race and NOT a long-lived-container symptom, ruling out the explanation given when these same failures were misattributed to ISS-0090 in PR #342 (which closed ISS-504).

root_cause.details: tests/integration/helpers.zig::runMigrationsForSchema() (used by TestHarness.init(), the harness most integration tests use) tracks applied migrations in a schema-local schema_migrations table that resolves via search_path to live inside the tenant schema itself. src/db/migrations.zig::Migrations.runForSchema() (the production migrator, called directly by some test files' own makePool(), and by provisionTenantSchema()) tracks applied migrations in public.schema_migrations keyed by (schema_name, version), per the explicit ISS-504 design decision. Both appliers run the same migration files against the same tenant_default schema, but a migration marked applied by one is invisible to the other, so the second tracker eventually re-applies a migration whose non-idempotent inline named constraint (uq_form_schema_field) has already been claimed by a downstream rename (migration 072), producing a deterministic 'already exists' failure independent of timing or container age.

files_to_change: tests/integration/helpers.zig -- runMigrationsForSchema/runMigrations: decide whether to delete this legacy local tracker in favor of calling the real Migrations.runForSchema(), or make it read/write public.schema_migrations instead of a schema-local copy
src/db/migrations.zig -- Migrations.runForSchema: no code change expected if the harness path is retired, but confirm behavior once harness path is fixed
tests/integration/iss102_claim_test.zig -- and any other test file with its own makePool() calling Migrations.runForSchema() directly -- not yet fully enumerated
src/design/iss504_migration_tracking.md -- note that the test harness's own bootstrapper violated the ISS-504 single-tracker decision and was not covered by ISS-504's verification scope

occurrences.context: Found while running zig build test-integration-iss102 to verify the ISS-0090 migration-051-trigger-idempotency and orphaned-tenant-schema-cleanup fixes on a byte-fresh db_test container (docker-compose down -v && up -d). Failure reproduced identically with zero concurrency, ruling out both the long-lived-container theory and the concurrent-test-threads theory offered in PR #342's description when it attributed the same failure signature to ISS-0090/#339.

prevention: When two subsystems both claim to track the same piece of state (here: which migrations have been applied to a schema), verify at design time that only one of them is ever actually consulted -- ISS-504 made the right call in principle (public.schema_migrations as single source of truth) but did not audit for a pre-existing second tracker already in the codebase (tests/integration/helpers.zig predates ISS-504).

Before attributing a newly-observed test failure to an existing open issue (as PR #342 did for ISS-0090), reproduce the failure under the conditions that would falsify the existing issue's stated root cause (e.g. single-threaded, freshly-recreated container) before writing the attribution into the PR description/CHANGELOG.
